post.headline: How Boomers ended up with half of America's wealth
post.caption: Boomers own almost half of all wealth in America, while Millennials own almost half of all debt. It started with 76 million babies, a country built around them, and a Congress that aged right along with them. Now $84 trillion is being passed down through 2045.
post.cta: Full story and interactive charts at the link in bio.

voiceover.transcript: Almost half of all wealth in America is owned by Boomers, while half of all debt is owned by Millennials. Boomers have spent the last half -century molding America in their image. Between 1946 and 1964, about seventy -six million babies were born in America. California was building one school a week in the fifties to keep up with that tremendous growth. In 1976, Boomers were old enough to run for Congress. They took over D .C. and never left. By 2013, they held 60 % of all wealth in America. They held 60 % of Congress while making up only a quarter of the population. Those lawmakers placed limits on new housing and created tax rules that favored existing wealth, making it hard for young generations to get ahead. Today Boomers own 41 % of all real estate wealth, often in multi -bedroom homes that are underutilized. More empty -nester boomers own homes with three or more bedrooms than Millennials with children. Millennials don't just own less, they also have more debt. Education costs have increased nine times since 1989. Now, the great generational wealth transfer is passing 84 trillion dollars from Boomers to wealthy children over the next few decades. But that wealth is concentrated too. At the top 10 % of Boomers hold 71 % of their generation's wealth. This is an opportunity to build in America with more housing, affordable education, and higher wages. You can read the full story on American inequality.
